project_scope.note: Built around the distinctive capsule and seed-support structures.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: If fruit is available, inspect the capsule: seeds are commonly supported by woody hook-like retinacula or jaculators.
family_diagnostics.leaves: Usually opposite and simple, without stipules.
family_diagnostics.flowers: Tubular and often zygomorphic; stamens usually 2 or 4.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Usually a 2-locular loculicidal capsule; seeds commonly rest on retinacula.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: The capsule and retinacula are a stronger family cue than flower shape.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Acanthaceae becomes memorable when you learn the capsule and its seed-support structures rather than trying to recognize yet another tubular flower.

steps.title: 1 · Start with a Ruellia flower
steps.look_for: Opposite leaves and a tubular bilateral flower.
steps.why_it_matters: Gets you into the correct Lamiales neighborhood.

steps.title: 2 · Wait for the capsule
steps.look_for: A dry capsule divided into two chambers.
steps.why_it_matters: Fruit architecture is stronger than flower color.

steps.title: 3 · Find the retinacula
steps.look_for: Woody hook-like structures that support the seeds inside the capsule.
steps.why_it_matters: Retinacula are the standout family mechanism.

steps.title: 4 · Watch the mature capsule open
steps.look_for: A mature capsule opening along its valves and releasing seeds.
steps.why_it_matters: Links the capsule structure to its dispersal function.

comparisons.title: Acanthaceae vs Plantaginaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have tubular bilateral flowers and capsules. Acanthaceae commonly has retinacula/jaculators; Plantaginaceae does not.

comparisons.title: Acanthaceae vs Lamiaceae
comparisons.rule: Lamiaceae commonly makes four nutlets; Acanthaceae makes a capsule.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not use flower shape alone; the capsule and retinacula are the stronger family tie-breakers.
